item.description:

item.title: block-and-file-storage-ebs-efs-fsx
item.description:
Block and File Storage: EBS, EFS and Amazon FSx Deep Dive#

S3 (Simple Storage Service) handles objects, but applications running on EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) or containers often need block storage (like a local hard drive) or shared file storage (NFS/SMB). Choosing the right storage type, volume tier, or FSx flavor is one of the most heavily tested topics on the SAA-C03 exam.

Block vs File vs Object at a glance#

flowchart TB
    s{Storage Requirement?}
    s -->|Single EC2 / low-latency DB disk| ebs[EBS / Instance Store]
    s -->|Shared Linux POSIX across AZs| efs[Amazon EFS]
    s -->|Windows SMB / AD share| fsxw[FSx for Windows]
    s -->|HPC / ML + S3 integration| fsxl[FSx for Lustre]
    s -->|Enterprise NetApp / multi-protocol| fsxn[FSx for NetApp ONTAP]
    s -->|HTTP REST / static / archive| s3[Amazon S3]

Amazon EBS (Elastic Block Store)#

EBS volumes are network-attached block disks locked to a single Availability Zone (AZ). To move a volume to another AZ, you snapshot it and restore in the target AZ.

item.title: caching-elasticache-cloudfront
item.description:
Caching: ElastiCache, CloudFront and DAX (DynamoDB Accelerator)#

The fastest query is the one you never make. Caching questions on the exam come down to: what layer (CDN, application, database) and which engine (Redis vs Memcached vs DAX).

Cache placement - pick the layer#

Latency source Fix
Static content far from users CloudFront (edge caching)
Repeated DB queries / session data ElastiCache in front of the DB
DynamoDB reads need microseconds DAX
API responses repeat API Gateway caching

ElastiCache: Redis vs Memcached#

Redis Memcached
Data structures Rich (lists, sets, sorted sets, streams) Simple key-value strings
Replication / failover Yes (Multi-AZ with auto failover) No
Persistence Yes (snapshots, AOF) No
Clustering Yes (cluster mode, sharding) Multi-threaded scaling
Pub/Sub, Lua, transactions Yes No
Typical use Session store, leaderboards, chat, queues Simple object caching

Exam shortcut: “failover / durability / data structures / sorted leaderboard” → Redis. “Pure cache, simplest and fastest horizontal scaling” → Memcached.

item.title: database-selection-matrix
item.description:
Database Selection Matrix#

The most common question format in Domain 3: “the application needs X - which database?” There are ~10 AWS database services and exactly one right answer per workload. Learn the workload → service mapping.

The decision table#

Workload Service Why
Relational OLTP (online transaction processing), joins, transactions, known schema RDS (Relational Database Service) (or Aurora for cloud-native scale) Managed SQL, Multi-AZ, replicas
Massive-scale key-value, any traffic shape, single-digit ms DynamoDB Serverless NoSQL, unlimited scale
Hot data, microsecond reads, session store ElastiCache (Redis/Memcached) In-memory
Data warehouse, OLAP (online analytical processing), columnar analytics Redshift Petabyte analytics
Interactive SQL on S3 (Simple Storage Service) data lake Athena Serverless, pay per query
Search, autocomplete, log analytics OpenSearch Full-text search
Document workloads, MongoDB-compatible DocumentDB Mongo API without Mongo ops
Graph relationships (social, fraud, routes) Neptune Graph DB
Time series (IoT, metrics) Timestream Built for timestamps
Immutable ledger / audit Aurora PostgreSQL / S3 Object Lock (Note: AWS deprecated QLDB on July 31, 2025) Cryptographic verifiability / WORM
In-memory cache with SQL on RDS-adjacent Redis Microsecond latency
Query exabytes in S3 directly from a data warehouse Redshift Spectrum Joins Redshift tables with S3 Parquet files without loading

RDS vs DynamoDB - the heavyweight bout#

item.title: dynamodb-deep-dive
item.description:
DynamoDB Deep Dive#

DynamoDB shows up in ~a third of all “which database” and “how do I scale reads” questions. The exam-level knowledge is: partitioning, capacity modes, indexes, DAX (DynamoDB Accelerator) and Global Tables.

Data model basics#

  • Table → items (rows) → attributes (columns) - schemaless except the key
  • Partition key (required) - hashed to decide storage partition; good partition keys spread load evenly
  • Composite key = partition key + sort key - enables range queries (WHERE orderId = X AND date BETWEEN...)
  • Item max size 400 KB
  • Access is via Query (key condition) or Scan (everything - avoid it)

Capacity modes#

On-demand Provisioned
Pricing Per request (pay per use) Per hour on WCU (write capacity unit)/RCU (read capacity unit) + autoscaling
Best for Unknown, spiky traffic Steady, predictable traffic
Scaling Instant, no planning Auto scaling policy on utilization
  • 1 WCU = 1 KB write per second; 1 RCU = 4 KB strongly consistent read per second (2x for eventually consistent)
  • Reads: eventually consistent by default (duplicates at read time possible), strongly consistent = 2x RCU

Indexes#

LSI (local secondary index) GSI (global secondary index)
Key Same partition key, new sort key Any key (new partition + sort)
Consistency Can be strongly consistent Always eventually consistent
Limits 5 per table 20 per table
Availability Same partition as item “Global” = separate index

Sparse index trick: items missing the indexed attribute are simply not in the index - filter by putting an attribute only on some items.

item.title: compute-performance-ec2-options
item.description:
Compute Performance: EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) Options#

“Which instance type / placement / purchase option” questions test whether you know the instance family alphabet and the three placement group shapes. (Pricing is covered in pricing-models.)

Instance families#

Family Optimized for Mnemonic
T (t3, t4g) Burstable general purpose (baseline CPU + credits) “t” = tiny/test
M (m5, m6i) Balanced general purpose “m” = middle
C (c5, c7g) Compute intensive (app servers, game servers, batch) “c” = compute
R (r5, x2idn) / X / Z Memory intensive (in-memory DB, caches, big data) “r” = RAM
P / G / VT / Inf GPU/ML training and inference “p/g” = graphics
Hpc / D High performance compute, high disk throughput
Mac macOS build farms

Burstable (T family) detail: instances earn CPU credits when idle and spend them under load; “unlimited” mode can pay for extra credits. “Variable low CPU baseline” → T family.

item.title: serverless-and-containers-lambda-ecs-eks
item.description:
Serverless & Containers: Lambda, RDS Proxy, API Gateway, ECS and EKS#

Modern architecture questions on SAA-C03 revolve around eliminating server management while respecting service limits, networking rules, and database connection pools.

AWS Lambda - limits, networking and scaling#

Hands-on: aws-lambda, lambda-api-gateway.

Hard limits the exam tests#

  • Max execution timeout: 15 minutes (900 seconds). If a job takes 25 minutes → use AWS Fargate or AWS Batch, never Lambda!
  • Memory: 128 MB to 10 GB — CPU and network bandwidth scale proportionally with memory. “A CPU-bound Lambda function is too slow” → increase its memory configuration.
  • Storage:
    • /tmp ephemeral storage: 512 MB default, configurable up to 10 GB (shared across warm invocations in the same execution environment — great for caching static reference files).
    • Need persistent shared storage across invocations or big ML models? Mount Amazon EFS (Elastic File System) (requires Lambda in a VPC).
  • Deployment package: 50 MB zipped (250 MB unzipped including Lambda Layers), or up to 10 GB as a container image from ECR (Elastic Container Registry).

Concurrency: Reserved vs Provisioned#

  • Default account concurrency limit: 1,000 concurrent executions per region (soft limit).
  • Reserved Concurrency: caps the max concurrency for one function so it can’t starve other functions (and guarantees that slice of capacity). Costs nothing extra; setting it to 0 throttles/disables the function.
  • Provisioned Concurrency: keeps N environments pre-initialized and warm → eliminates cold starts for latency-sensitive APIs (costs money).

Lambda in a VPC & the RDS Proxy pattern#

flowchart LR
    apigw[API Gateway] --> lambda[Lambda in Private Subnet]
    lambda -->|pooled connections| proxy[Amazon RDS Proxy]
    proxy --> rds[(RDS / Aurora Multi-AZ)]
    lambda -->|outbound internet via| nat[NAT Gateway]
  1. Lambda in a VPC has NO internet access by default (even in a “public” subnet, Lambda ENIs (Elastic Network Interface) never get public IPs!). To call an external public API from a VPC-connected Lambda, put Lambda in a Private Subnet with a route to a NAT Gateway.
  2. The RDS connection storm problem: Lambda scales out to 1,000 concurrent instances in seconds; each opens a DB connection and crashes RDS (Too many connections).
    • The fix: Amazon RDS Proxy (placed in the VPC between Lambda and RDS/Aurora).
    • Pools and shares DB connections, enforces IAM (Identity and Access Management) authentication with credentials stored in Secrets Manager, and reduces Multi-AZ failover time by up to 66% by preserving client connections during failover.

Sınav Tuzağı (Exam Trap): “Lambda fonksiyonları trafik patlamasında RDS veritabanında bağlantı hatası (Too many connections / connection exhaustion) veriyor” sorusunun cevabı Read Replica veya daha büyük RDS değil, Amazon RDS Proxy‘dir!

item.title: data-transfer-and-hybrid-services
item.description:
Data Transfer and Hybrid Services#

Moving data is its own question family: “we have 500 TB on-premises, get it to S3 (Simple Storage Service)” or “users must still write to a local file server”. Each answer is a specific service - and mixing them up is easy, so learn the one job per service.

The transfer service lineup#

Service Job Scenario keyword
DataSync Scheduled bulk transfer (NFS/SMB/HDFS/object → S3/EFS (Elastic File System)/FSx) “migrate file shares”, “agent, scheduled, fast”
Transfer Family Managed SFTP / FTPS / FTP endpoints backed by S3/EFS “partners upload via SFTP”
Storage Gateway Hybrid: local file/volume/tape interface → S3/EBS-backed “on-prem apps keep using local protocols”
Snow Family Physically ship petabytes “no bandwidth / 100 TB+”
AWS Backup Centralized backup plans “tag-based backup across services”

Storage Gateway modes (classic exam trio)#

  • File Gateway - NFS/SMB share backed by S3 objects (“local file share, objects in S3”)
  • Volume Gateway - iSCSI block storage; cached (hot data local, everything in S3) vs stored (full copy local, async backup to EBS (Elastic Block Store) snapshots)
  • Tape Gateway - virtual tape library (VTL) for legacy backup software

Snow Family#

Device Scale Notes
Snowcone ~8-14 TB, rugged edge device Edge computing + transfer
Snowball Edge 80-210 TB The standard “ship a box” answer
Snowmobile 100 PB per truck Exabyte-scale, literally a shipping container

“Petabytes of data, limited bandwidth” → Snowball. “Ongoing streaming” → Kinesis / DataSync instead.
